title: Non-empty Intersection
statement: Five random intervals are generated within the interval [0,1]. Each interval is formed by independently selecting two points uniformly at random from [0,1], and taking the smaller as the left endpoint and the larger as the right endpoint. What is the probability that all five intervals share a common (non-empty) intersection?

title: Standing Table I
statement: Three points are chosen independently and uniformly at random on the circumference of a circular table. Legs are attached at those five points. What is the probability that the table stands? [NOTE: source text is internally inconsistent - says three points then five points]

title: Game Of Chords
statement: Forty points are placed evenly around the circumference of a circle. Alice and Bob take turns drawing chords between two distinct points. A new chord must not intersect any existing chord in the interior of the circle, though it may meet other chords at points on the circumference. Alice moves first. The player who cannot draw a legal chord on their turn loses. Under optimal play which player has a winning strategy?

title: Unequal Neighbors
statement: Given an m*n grid of random integers, each cell can have its value increased by at most 1. A cell is a neighbor of another if they share a side. Determine whether it is possible to modify any grid so that no cell has the same value as any of its neighbors.

title: Find The Units Digit
statement: Consider every 100-digit number (including leading zeros), i.e. all integers from 0 to 10^100 - 1. For each, compute the product of its nonzero digits (treat the product for zero as 1). Sum these products over all 10^100 numbers. What is the last decimal digit of the sum?

title: Ship Destroyer
statement: Sixteen ships occupy the cells of a 4x4 grid. You have four bombs, each landing independently and uniformly at random in one of the 16 cells (with repetition). A bomb destroys every ship in its row and its column. What is the probability that after all four bombs, every ship has been destroyed?

title: Moving The Piece I
statement: Given a grid with 183 rows and 181 columns, Alice and Bob take turns moving a piece to an adjacent square (diagonals count as adjacent). Once a square is visited it cannot be revisited. The piece starts on the top-left square, which also cannot be revisited. The loser is the player with no legal move. Alice goes first; who has a winning strategy?

title: Even Marbles Everywhere
statement: Each square on an 8x8 grid is randomly filled with a black or white marble. What is the probability that the number of white marbles in EVERY row and EVERY column is even?

title: Hard Grid Arrangement
statement: Consider an n*n grid where each cell is filled with 0 or 1. How many arrangements are there such that the sum of the cells in every 2x2 sub-grid equals 2? Closed form in n; answer for n = 10.

title: All Odds Before Even
statement: You roll a fair 6-sided die repeatedly. What is the probability that all odd values (1, 3, 5) appear before any even value (2, 4, 6)?

title: Standing Table II
statement: Five points are chosen independently and uniformly at random on the circumference of a circular table. Legs are attached at those five points. What is the probability that the table stands?

title: 10 Consecutive Heads
statement: What is the expected number of flips required to obtain 10 consecutive heads when flipping a fair coin?

title: Chords Intersection I
statement: If 10 chords are drawn on a circle with endpoints chosen uniformly at random along the circumference, what is the expected number of intersections?

title: 1 Leftward Jump
statement: A frog begins on the first stone of seven stones numbered 1 to 7 left to right. Each move it hops to a stone it has not already landed on. What is the probability that after touching all stones the frog made precisely one jump to the left?

title: Marble Swap II
statement: You have 3 marbles: red, blue, red, in that order. Each move you randomly select two distinct marbles and swap them. After 10 moves, what is the probability the marbles are back in original order (red, blue, red)?

title: Scary Permutation
statement: How many permutations of {1..9} are there such that every number after the first has at least one number somewhere to its left differing from it by exactly 1?

title: Grid Frog I
statement: A 2x8 grid has one frog in each of its 16 cells. Simultaneously every frog jumps to a side-adjacent cell. After all jumps exactly one frog must occupy each cell again. In how many ways can this happen?

title: At Least Six I
statement: You roll a fair six-sided die repeatedly, keeping a running total. Let T be the number of rolls needed for the running total to reach or exceed 6. What is E[T]?

title: Game Of Placing Knights
statement: Alice and Bob take turns placing knights on an 8x8 chessboard. A knight cannot be placed on an occupied square nor on a square attacked by an existing knight. A player loses with no legal move. Alice first; who has a winning strategy?

title: Same Arc I
statement: N points are selected independently and uniformly at random on the circumference of a circle. What is the probability that all N points lie within some semicircular arc, given N > 2? Answer for N = 10.

title: Increasing Dice Rolls III
statement: A fair six-sided die is rolled twice, outcomes recorded in order. What is the probability that the second roll is strictly larger than the first?

title: Fill In The Blanks
statement: Consider 1_2_3_4_5_6_7_8_9 where each blank is filled with + or - with equal probability 1/2. What is the probability the final result equals 0?

title: Exponent Perfect Square
statement: How many integers p between 100 and 400 inclusive satisfy that p^p is a perfect square?

title: Odd Heads II
statement: You toss 100 coins. 99 are biased showing heads with probability p; the remaining one is fair. What is the probability of an odd number of heads in terms of p? Answer for p = 0.10.

title: Dice Rolls Product
statement: A fair six-sided die is rolled 10 times. For each face i let N_i be the number of times side i appears. Compute E[N_1 N_2 N_3 N_4 N_5 N_6].

title: Jumping Frog V
statement: A frog begins at point 0 and must reach point 10. The frog can only jump more than 1 point at a time. How many unique ways can the frog travel from 0 to 10?

title: Dot Product
statement: Two 10-dimensional vectors. Each entry of the first is 0 or 1 with equal probability. Each entry of the second is 1 with probability 3/4 and 0 with probability 1/4, independently. What is the probability the dot product is odd?

title: Marble Swap I
statement: You have 3 marbles: red, blue, green, in that order. Each move you randomly select two distinct marbles and swap them. After 125 moves, what is the probability they are back in original order?

title: Monster Escape I
statement: Mario starts at the bottom-left of a 100x100 grid, a monster at the bottom-right. Every second both move simultaneously to one of four neighboring squares. If they occupy the same square Mario dies. What is the probability Mario survives 1000 seconds?

title: Chords Forming Quadrilateral
statement: Given 8 points on a circle, draw all chords connecting each pair. Then 4 chords are randomly selected. What is the probability these 4 chords form a convex quadrilateral?

title: Monster Escape II
statement: Mario starts at (0,0), a monster at (4,4). Each second Mario moves up or right with equal probability (constrained at the border of the 4x4 grid); the monster moves down or left similarly. What is the probability they meet before reaching opposite corners?

title: Matrix Attack III
statement: Let A be a 7x7 integer matrix where each column contains 1..7 exactly once and a_ij = a_ji for all i,j. What is the probability that the main diagonal entries also form a permutation of 1..7?

title: Bulbs In A Grid
statement: A 3x3 grid of light bulbs, each independently on with probability 1/2. Calculate the probability that no two side-adjacent bulbs are on simultaneously.

title: Chess Tournament III
statement: Alice and Bob compete in a 32-participant chess tournament. Each round randomly pairs remaining players; each match is a coin flip and the loser is eliminated. What is the probability Alice and Bob face each other during the tournament?

title: Count Paths II
statement: How many paths lead from (0,0) to (8,10) using only unit right or up moves, where it is prohibited to pass through points (x,y) with both x and y odd?

title: Five Light Bulbs
statement: Five light bulbs are initially all off. Every second one bulb is chosen uniformly at random and flipped. What is the expected time until all five bulbs are off again?

title: Letter-envelope Pairing
statement: We have 10 pairs of gloves, each left glove randomly paired with a right glove, numbered 1 to 10. What is the probability that for every pair the absolute difference between left and right glove numbers is at most 1?

title: Frog Return
statement: A grasshopper jumps along a line. Its first jump is 1 cm, second 2 cm, and so on. Each jump is left or right. What is the probability it returns to its starting position on the 25th jump?

title: Direction Change I
statement: Bob travels from (0,0) to (16,16) moving one unit in the positive x or y direction at a time, all paths equally likely. What is the probability he changes direction an odd number of times?

title: 3 Dice Minimum
statement: What is the expected value of the smallest number rolled when three fair 100-sided dice are rolled?

title: Game On Divisors III
statement: Alice and Bob play with a pile of 2025 stones. On a turn a player removes any positive number of stones that divides the current pile size. The player who takes the last stone loses. Alice first; who has a winning strategy?

title: Jumping Frog IV
statement: A frog begins at point 0 and may jump an odd number of points each move. How many unique ways can the frog reach point 10?

title: Dice Game III
statement: Six players numbered 1-6. Player 1 rolls a die; rolling a 1 wins and ends the game, otherwise the die passes to the player matching the roll. A player rolling his own number wins. Calculate the probability Player 1 wins.

title: 105 Pebbles
statement: Three piles contain 5, 49, and 51 pebbles. Allowed operations: merge any two piles, or divide a pile with an even count into two equal piles. Is it possible to reach 105 piles of exactly one pebble each?

title: Missing Pairwise Product
statement: Four positive reals a,b,c,d. The products of each pair form the set {9,10,12,27,30,x}. Determine x.

title: Constrained Subsets II
statement: How many subsets of {1,2,...,30} have element sum greater than 232?

title: Fifth Card
statement: Five cards are drawn from a standard 52-card deck and you see all five. You arrange them and reveal the first four face up so your friend can always determine the fifth. You may agree a strategy beforehand. Find a strategy that achieves this.

title: Expected Area
statement: Two integers X and Y are chosen independently and uniformly from {1,2,3,4,5}. They are the legs of a right triangle with vertices (0,0), (X,0), (0,Y). What is the expected area?

title: Difficult Die Constraints
statement: You roll a fair six-sided die repeatedly until both a 2 and a 3 have appeared at least once. What is the probability that exactly two 6s occur during this entire process?

title: Game Of Discarding Cards
statement: A 52-card deck. Players turn over two cards at a time: both black go to the dealer's pile, both red to the player's pile, mixed are discarded. Repeated for 26 pairs. If the player ends with more cards than the dealer they win $10, otherwise (including ties) nothing. What is the fair value of this game?

title: Normal Inequality IV
statement: Let X and Y be independent standard normal random variables. Determine P(Y > 4X).

title: Ants On A Circle I
statement: Nine ants equally spaced around a circle. Each independently chooses clockwise or counterclockwise and moves at constant speed, making one full revolution per minute if uninterrupted. Meeting ants instantly reverse. Ants are indistinguishable. What is the probability that after one minute the set of occupied points equals the nine starting points?

title: Ants On A Circle II
statement: Same setup as Ants On A Circle I with nine ants, but the ants are distinguishable. What is the probability that after one minute every ant is exactly at its own starting point?

title: Ants On A Circle III
statement: Same setup but with ten distinguishable ants. What is the probability that after one minute every ant is exactly at its own starting point?

title: Game Of Evaluation
statement: The numbers 1 through 100 are written in a row. Alice and Bob alternately fill an empty space between consecutive numbers with +, -, or x. The final expression is evaluated with standard order of operations. Alice wins if the value is odd, else Bob. Alice first; who has a winning strategy?

title: Ant On A Cube I
statement: An ant starts at one corner of a cube and moves only along edges, choosing a random edge each time. What is the expected number of edges traversed before reaching the opposite vertex?

title: Dice Game VII
statement: You roll a fair six-sided die once and record the number, then keep rolling until you get a result different from the first roll. Your payout is the sum of all numbers rolled including the first and the final differing roll. What is the expected payout?

title: Duck Escape
statement: A duck sits at the center of a circular lake. A fox on the shore cannot swim and moves around the lake at four times the duck's swimming speed. The duck can fly only once it reaches the shore. Can the duck always reach the shore without being eaten?

title: Count Regions I
statement: Determine the maximum number of regions into which a plane can be divided using n straight lines. Answer for n = 10.

title: Count Regions III
statement: Determine the maximum number of regions into which 3-dimensional space can be divided using n planes. Answer for n = 10.
